title: preprocessing.curate_data.curate_weather
---



```python
preprocessing.curate_data.curate_weather(weather_df, data, forecast_horizon)
```

Checks if the weather dataframe has the correct shape.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                           | Description                               | Default    |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|------------|
| weather_df       | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | DataFrame containing weather information. | _required_ |
| data             | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | The main dataset.                         | _required_ |
| forecast_horizon | [int](`int`)                                   | The forecast horizon in hours.            | _required_ |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#a4ecede6 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.preprocessing.curate_data import curate_weather

FORECAST_HORIZON = 24
n_data = 48
data = pd.DataFrame(
    {"load": range(n_data)},
    index=pd.date_range("2023-01-01", periods=n_data, freq="h", tz="UTC"),
)
weather_df = pd.DataFrame(
    {"temp": range(n_data + FORECAST_HORIZON)},
    index=pd.date_range(
        "2023-01-01", periods=n_data + FORECAST_HORIZON, freq="h", tz="UTC"
    ),
)
curate_weather(weather_df, data, forecast_horizon=FORECAST_HORIZON)
assert weather_df.shape[0] == data.shape[0] + FORECAST_HORIZON
print("weather_df shape is correct:", weather_df.shape[0] == data.shape[0] + FORECAST_HORIZON)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
weather_df shape is correct: True
```
:::
:::


## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

If the weather dataframe does not have the expected number of rows, a
diagnostic message describing the mismatch is logged via ``print`` and
the function returns ``None`` without raising.
